feature: a package.json project is JavaScript when its sources are

specs.description: A package.json project with only JavaScript sources is javascript.
specs.given: a project with package.json and src/index.js, no TypeScript and no tsconfig.json

specs.description: A project with any TypeScript source stays typescript, JavaScript beside it or not.
specs.given: a project with package.json, src/a.ts and src/b.js
specs.then: Its language line reads typescript (package.json), not javascript.

specs.description: A tsconfig.json at the root keeps a project typescript before it has a source.
specs.given: a project with package.json, a root tsconfig.json and src/a.js only

specs.description: A package.json with no source is typescript, as before.
specs.given: a project with only a package.json

specs.description: hexa doctor names the same language.
specs.given: a project with package.json and src/index.js, and one with package.json and src/a.ts
specs.then: The type line reads javascript (package.json) for the first and typescript (package.json) for the second.

specs.description: The session-start fingerprint names the same language.
specs.given: a project with package.json and src/index.js
specs.when: the session-start hook prints its project block

specs.description: The session-start fingerprint still names typescript for a TypeScript project.
specs.given: a project with package.json and src/a.ts
specs.when: the session-start hook prints its project block

specs.description: Beside a Python manifest, JavaScript sources list javascript.
specs.given: a project with a pyproject.toml, package.json and src/index.js and no TypeScript
specs.then: Its language line lists javascript (package.json) and python (pyproject.toml).

specs.description: Beside a Python manifest, a package.json that is tooling only is not listed.
specs.given: a project with a pyproject.toml and a package.json and no JavaScript or TypeScript source
specs.then: Its language line lists python only.

specs.description: JavaScript in node_modules or in analyze.exclude does not make a project javascript.
specs.given: a project with a package.json whose only JavaScript is under node_modules and in a path listed in analyze.exclude

specs.description: A test file does not make a project javascript, and a source file does.
specs.given: a project with package.json, src/a.test.js and src/index.js
specs.then: Its language line reads javascript (package.json); with src/index.js removed it reads typescript (package.json).

specs.description: The layer inventory's language column is unchanged for JavaScript files.
specs.given: a JavaScript project with files in layers
specs.then: Each layer_inventory row for those files names language typescript, as before.

specs.description: The label change moves no grade, score or finding.
specs.then: The grade is A+, the score is 100 and there are no violations or dead exports.

specs.description: The Rust, Go and Python labels are unchanged.
specs.given: a Rust, a Go and a Python scaffold
specs.then: The language lines read rust (Cargo.toml), go (go.mod) and python (pyproject.toml).

specs.description: Naming JavaScript does not depend on the order of the files.
specs.given: a JavaScript project and a shuffle of the order its files are written in

specs.description: The TypeScript scaffold keeps its label and its grade.
specs.then: Its language line reads typescript (package.json) and the grade is A+.

specs.description: The inventory gains no javascript row.
specs.then: No layer_inventory row names the language javascript, and the files of a mixed project are not split between two rows by extension.
